context: The endpoint hashes JSON.stringify(req.body) - a re-serialisation of the body the framework already parsed - instead of the bytes that arrived. The two existing tests stay green because each one signs a string it produced with JSON.stringify itself, so the parse-and-re-stringify round trip is a no-op for those payloads. It stops being a no-op the moment the real payload contains an escape the serialiser writes differently: the captured delivery carries \u00e0, \u2014 and escaped forward slashes, all of which come back as literal characters after a round trip, changing the bytes and therefore the HMAC. Predicted baseline failure: the agent treats this as a signature or encoding puzzle rather than a raw-body one - it reaches for charset handling, re-escapes the payload before hashing, normalises unicode, or accepts one of the two invitations in the request. Both invitations are traps with an anti-pattern behind them. Answering 200 on an unverified delivery is the webhook-replay hole the verification exists to close, and the clock story is a red herring the incident notes settle: the 400 rate was unchanged after NTP was fixed, so widening or removing the freshness window buys nothing and removes replay protection. Its regression test is predicted to be a freshly built ASCII payload signed at test time, which passes against the broken code and the fixed code alike and so proves nothing.
